text:
maria park: starting a tiny canary for kaito11b-int4; noticed weird first-token tail latency and a couple of OOMs during warmups. posting notes so we don't re-run the same blind experiments.
noah li: can you paste a minimal trace? is this cold compile or allocation failure?
maria park: short log snippet:
```
[2026-03-21T09:12:01Z] serve: req=xyz01 model=kaito11b-int4
[2026-03-21T09:12:01Z] runtime: kv_allocate 192MB -> ok
[2026-03-21T09:12:01Z] runtime: prefetch schedule slots=5 cost=270ms
[2026-03-21T09:12:01Z] runtime: cuda malloc scratch 1.1GB -> OOM
[2026-03-21T09:12:02Z] runtime: eviction triggered, retry -> success
[2026-03-21T09:12:02Z] decode: token0 latency=480ms
```
samir rao: looks similar to the delta we saw on ember7b; prefetch slots + int4 kernel workspaces caused transient high watermarks. what's the canary config?
maria park: canary defaults: batch=6, max_new_tokens=220, prefetch=5, kernel-cache=off.
noah li: immediate suggestions: 1) drop batch -> 3 2) limit max_new_tokens -> 120 3) set prefetch=1 4) kernel-cache=on 5) enable hetero-fp-final for final linear. can you try a quick rollout?
maria park: will try patch: `./canary_launch --batch 3 --max-new 120 --prefetch 1 --kernel-cache on --hetero-fp-final`
ops-hound: note: fragmentation_defrag=15s and cuda_cushion=0.05 are recommended for int4 pools; adding policy to canary node.
samir rao: also consider enabling `quant-stochastic-rounding=true` in runtime flags; it reduced repetition and truncation on long outputs in our prior runs.
maria park: curious about warmstart behavior — is there an easy way to pre-populate kernels + kv to avoid the 1st-token spike?
oah li: use `warmup_prompts=6 --prewarm=true` in the canary job; run a few short prompts that trigger typical path lengths. that populates kernel cache + warms allocator arenas.
infra-bot: deploying `kaito11b-int4-canary-20260321a` to 2x GPUs with config {batch:3,max_new:120,prefetch:1,kernel_cache:on,hetero_fp_final:true}. heatmaps and allocation traces enabled.
maria park: deployed; running warmup. will monitor allocation graph.
ops-hound: also enabled a runtime fallback rule: if scratch allocation > 900MB try evict-kv then fallback to fp16 for that request. logging enabled under /logs/canaries/kaito11b-int4.
infra-bot: canary metrics (10m): memory high-water reduced 22%, first-token p50 dropped from 480ms->160ms, OOMs 0/10. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/canaries/kaito11b-int4-canary-20260321a
maria park: ramping to 10m smoke now; collecting eval diffs for QA dataset to check quality regressions. will post results.
samir rao: if we still see small quality delta vs fp16, try hetero-fp-final + stochastic rounding together; that combo was the sweet spot on nova experiments.
maria park: ack. thanks everyone. will update after the 1h smoke. :white_check_mark:
